neighboring room. As you look around,
you get the impression that this mine
seems to have been abandoned quite
suddenly and hastily: some miners' tools
are still lying scattered about the
ground... Apparently they had planned to
widen this tunnel to go further into the
interior of the mountain - but the
little success of the work so far can
already be measured by the few pieces of
rubble that have been broken out of the
rugged rock face, so that the only way
out of this dead end leads to the east,
i.e. back to the former mint.
[on a path]

230.text: You enter a small cave whose ceiling is supported against the rocky floor with massive wooden beams. When this country was once financially strong, this area represented the coin in which the country's customary hard currency was minted. Apparently the usual rabble has once again removed everything valuable from here - although: there is still a hearth back there, in which the fire is still burning, over the flames of which hangs a small cauldron with molten silver! When you look around the cave a little more closely, aroused by this discovery, you can also discover some vessels that were probably intended for storing and transporting the minted coins! The exit to the outside is directly behind you to the south, while to the west there is another small tunnel, which, however, ends after a few meters on a rock face...

231.text: When you enter the monastery garden, you are taken aback: It won't be that easy to push your way through this undergrowth! Everything around you is overgrown - actually quite understandable, since nobody has taken care of this garden for decades. To put it bluntly (The gardener - if he's still alive - may forgive us...): This place looks more like a jungle than the carefully tended garden where, a long, long time ago, the monks of this monastery had dedicated to their meditations! But as you brutally force your way through the thorny undergrowth, you suddenly come across a wrought-iron gate that at first glance was hidden by the undergrowth! As you look through the bars, you shudder: This is the gate that leads directly to the cemetery of the monastery, where all the dead of the village used to be buried! But something is wrong with this place: dense wafts of fog creep sluggishly and ominously across the floor of the graveyard, but strangely do not penetrate the bars of the gate, but almost seem to be held back by a magical barrier. When you see that the mist seems to come straight out of the partly open and desecrated graves - almost as if the spirits of the dead wanted to flee their final resting place to take revenge on all living things - a chill runs down your spine. .. If you have the right key with you, you can enter the cemetery in the north - if you still have the courage to do so... If not, the small archway in the east will lead you back to the monastery.

232.text: You enter the dining room of the monastery. A long time ago, the monks used to sit here every evening to eat and drink. Oh yes, indeed: it must be a really damn long time ago, because all the dining tables and benches are either broken on the floor or covered in rat droppings in such a way that you would hate to even touch them! Your impression gets stronger: this monastery has been deserted in a hurry - you're just wondering why... Exits lead in all directions except to the east.

233.text: Unnoticed you reach the throne room of the elf king Firon: blinded by the bright light reflected from the walls, you shield your eyes with your hands and look around in amazement: as huge as the throne room is, it is also empty: the only ones "Furniture" that you can recognize is Firon's throne of ice and the many glittering ice crystals that hang tens of meters from the ceiling and reflect the incoming sunlight in every imaginable color - as if they themselves were made of a gigantic, infinitely precious precious crystal. .

234.text: Unfortunately, you decided to explore the frozen desert much deeper than was actually necessary. Well, blinded by the extremely bright sunlight, you unfortunately missed the crack in the ground directly in front of you - and stumbled straight into a deep glacier! Um, what more can I say about that? You should consider yourself lucky not to have starved to death, because entering this frozen wasteland without fast transportation is in itself certain death! But don't give up: Maybe one day you will be found and thawed out by a few scientists - younger and fresher than your peers will then be...

235.text: You continue your way through the cemetery, although you ask yourself with a rather unpleasant feeling in your stomach why everything around you has suddenly become so quiet... In the north you can see the silhouette of a against the sickly yellow light of the full moon old burial vault, when the ominous silence is suddenly interrupted by a long, wild scream that makes your blood run cold: This scream was anything but human! But before you can think again, you hear a second - HUMAN - scream, which after a few seconds turns into a low whimpering, until it finally dies away completely... When you break out of your terrified shivering, you notice a hoarse hiss and the cracking of some branches behind you - and it's coming straight at you! So we should take our shaky legs in hand and either seek refuge in the crypt in the north, or flee to the chapel in the eastern part of the cemetery!

236.text: With mixed feelings you enter the cemetery of the old monastery, while the gate in the southern wall squeaks terribly on its hinges - as if it were being moved by the freezing wind, which strangely seems to have picked up at the very moment you entered the cemetery have. You shiver as you look down and see the billowing cold mist creeping up your legs. In the meantime it has become so foggy that you can hardly see the ground. Tentatively you put one foot after the other into this gray sea and follow the path towards the small chapel to the north, past weather-beaten tombstones and overturned wrought-iron crosses that seem to reach out to you in the eerie light like claws frozen in agony. .. -Hey, freak! Tell me, don't you actually have a watch, or are you blind? You're standing here in a cemetery, it's just after midnight - and WE HAVE A FULL MOON! If the rest of this game sucks as well as the story so far suggests, something pretty bad is about to happen! Okay: if you're actually planning to take a little walk around here - please: nobody's holding you back - but please don't expect me to share your somewhat macabre hobbies with you! I'll wait here for you - MAYBE...! Oh, by the way: Have you already seen the open grave back there...?

237.text: This is - or better: WAR - the old monastery smithy, in which weapons, armor and objects of daily use were manufactured in the past. Many of the items are still lying around: for example, there are still some old, but still reasonably working-looking weapons hanging on the walls, and there is also an old anvil here, on which the blacksmith's hammer has rusted over the years. The only way out of the forge is south, back into the monks' dining room.

238.text: You enter the king's burial vault. Hardly a ray of light falls through the small, barred hatch in the west wall. Right in the center of the tomb stands the king's mighty sarcophagus, adorned with scenes from his glorious and active life... The only way out of this dark and spooky room is through the door in the south wall, back to the moonlit graveyard...

239.text: You are standing in a small chapel, but in contrast to the rest of the monastery it is still quite well preserved. In the twilight of the chapel you can barely make out a few stone steps that lead down into a small crypt next to the confessional... The large door in the south leads you back to the cemetery, while you can climb down the steps into the darkness. ..

240.text: This appears to be Mylgor's bedchamber. It really is by far the most tastefully furnished room in this house: an ornate bed stands against the north wall, with a small bedside table next to it. On the walls you can see some precious old oil paintings. The only exit is through the door in the east wall, back to the corridor...

241.text: You come out into a short hallway, lit only by a few blazing torches mounted on the black-washed walls. In the north wall there is a massive, with "Laboratory - trespassing prohibited!" labeled steel door. A pair of crampons lead back upstairs, back into Mylgor's fireplace room. You can now either try to enter the laboratory behind the north wall or the room to the west. Of course, you are also free to climb on the crampons and get back to the fireplace room above Mylgor's secret hideout...

242.text: As the sign on the door indicated, this is Mylgor's secret laboratory: it's overflowing with test tubes, flasks and measuring cups, filled with all sorts of mysterious liquids bubbling up in every imaginable color. You have to concentrate very hard in order not to be confused by this sudden flood of new impressions - but then you see him: MYLGOR, the malicious alchemist, the vassal of the great evil, whose name you don't even dare to utter in your mind! When your eyes meet, his face twists into a malicious grimace: he slowly approaches you, shows you a huge horse syringe that he has just filled with a greenish, bubbling poison, and snarls: "You didn't follow my orders , my dear, right...?" You hastily look around for possible escape routes, but can't see anything apart from the huge steel door to the south...!

244.text: When the orc father happily sees his little son entering the cave behind you, his initially hostile gaze suddenly turns into a broad grin. "Oho! Looks like we're going to have company for dinner today!", he says, and you wince involuntarily - but he continues undeterred in his rough-bellied manner, without even realizing the ambiguity of his words : "Well, if my wife should actually manage to grill the lizard before we all starve to death, you can have lunch with us. Just sit down - there's enough for all of us!" With very mixed feelings, you sit down on one of the small stools, trying frantically not to look at the animal over the fireplace...

245.text: While you wait for your lunch, you and the orc father look at the little child who is sitting in the corner of the cave and is overjoyed playing with the crystal ball that you gave him. Suddenly it slips through his fingers! The little one immediately jumps after it and chases it through the entire cave, squealing and screaming happily - until he finally catches it with a death-defying dive just in front of the fireplace! But at the same moment the boy's fingers close around the ball, he gets caught right between the legs of his mother, who was just setting the table, so that she trips over her child and sends the entire dish clattering on his back! Sitting in the middle of a huge pile of broken glass, the little orc begins to scream loudly, and when the father briefly misses a glance, the mother steps up to her son and, to top it all off, gives him a hard left straight. That helps: the orc child, taken aback, stops screaming and looks around embarrassedly... For a brief moment, the entire orc family looks down angrily at their son, who is picking the last shards out of his fur with an unhappy expression, and he is completely distracted from you...

246.text: After you have entered the servants' room, Mylgor sticks his head through the door gap again, wishes you a good night's sleep, leaves the room - and locks the door behind him!

247.text: When you have returned the contract and the knife to the man, his face disappears behind the hatch. After a few seconds you hear the door being unlocked from the inside. "Come in!" says the man when he opens the door for you and leads you into a small but very comfortably furnished room with a fireplace. He introduces himself as "Mylgor, Alchemist" and shows you the room where you should spend the night. When you ask where he wants to sleep if not there, he laughs heartily and says: "Do you really think that this little hut is big enough for a scientist like me to live in? No, but not: This is just the room where my servant usually sleeps, but who is currently running some errands for me in the neighboring village. My lab and the other rooms are... - hidden! It doesn't matter where..." Mylgor nervously strokes his goatee, but then forces himself back into his peculiar smile. "But I actually thought we wanted to talk about you - not about me...?", he says and nods his head in the direction of the fireplace room, "Let's chat for an hour by the warm fireplace, and maybe I'll tell you a little tell us about the history of our village. But first give me your wet clothes - otherwise you could easily catch your death...!" With a very queasy feeling in your stomach, you undress, but keep a close eye on the old alchemist: who knows what kind of favor you are supposed to do for the old man? Wasn't there a greedy twinkle in his eyes? To be on the safe side, you peek at the door of your chamber: thank God! It can be locked! Embarrassed and unsure, you hand Mylgor your damp swimming trunks, but all he does is put them by the fireplace to dry...

248.text: When you enter the fireplace room again, you wonder why Mylgor actually didn't lock the door. Something in this house doesn't seem right - not at all right... You also wonder why Mylgor isn't there to greet you: maybe this is just a trap, because he has noticed that you Didn't keep your promise to eliminate Firon? Or maybe King Richard and his brother didn't tell you the full truth and had Mylgor killed before you could see through them and right your mistake of letting Firon live? You have strong doubts and pangs of conscience when you consider that it was your fault that an innocent person had to die...

249.text: In the middle of the clearing, a little orc boy is playing "ant bomber", a hunting game very popular among the orcs. He appears to be around eighty years old and not fully grown yet - but give it a few more centuries and he will easily strangle you with his left hand. You watch the child play for a few moments: his right hand hovers high in the air over an ant hole, while with his left he shoos the wood ants crawling around on the ground towards the hole. Every time an ant tries to slip into its burrow, the little one drops a pebble on it! However, the young orc doesn't seem to have had much luck in this game so far, you reassuredly remark as he growls contritely in the face of an ant that he missed just before the hole: "Okay, 23:4 for you! But now It's going well, people!" At some point you get tired of watching the orc do his sadistic machinations and approach him. When he notices you, the little one hands you a few pebbles: "Here! Let's make a match: I'll bet two gold pieces!" Without accepting his offer, you take the pebbles from the boy's hand and forcefully throw them into the bushes. The orc seems to understand, puffs and murmurs: "Then dont..."

Unable to move, you have to watch as he silently grows bigger and bigger... Hissing hoarsely and with outstretched arms, he starts moving - step by step, because he's in no hurry... But suddenly he stops! For fractions of a second, your eyes meet and you can feel the lust for murder and the abysmal hatred blazing in his eyes...

When you try to touch her - she turns to dust...

As long as I have I've been waiting for this moment, and it's about time we got over it...", he answers you in a soft voice, the melody of which resonates with something like melancholy and resignation...

355.text: Firon replies, "To prove to you that I'm on your side, I'm going to give you a key, the purpose of which I'm sure will be explained to you later. Unfortunately, I don't have the authority to tell you personally, but there is someone ... -someone in the old monastery on the hill in the northeast of the country that you should find. We both were members of a lobby that secretly dealt with the country's problems after evil took over. Regrettably ..." - with these words he sighs and absent-mindedly looks past you into the cold emptiness for a short moment - "Unfortunately he didn't manage to flee to us in this desert, so that he escaped to the captors of evil in the Hands fell... I never saw him again, nor the monastery that then served as our secret headquarters: all I had was a key, the imprint of which I cast in magical ice and kept for decades. May he help you in your quest..." With these words, Firon stands up, takes a large key from a secret compartment in his throne and places it carefully in your outstretched hand. With a look at the portal behind you, he adds : "My guards will let you pass. I will instruct them to get one of my fastest badger sleds ready for your return to the edge of the ice regions. Farewell, my friend - and may the gods protect you..." With these words, Firon beckons to the Yeti, who will lead you outside, where Firon's sleigh is already waiting for you...

357.text: The king's ghost looks at you for a while, then hops onto the edge of his coffin with a mischievous grin, and after making himself comfortable there, he begins to tell you the history of his kingdom: "A long, long time ago ", he begins his story, and his face is again that of an old, bitter man, "this was a beautiful, peaceful and prosperous country, in which all my subjects were justly and wisely ruled by me. I resided in my castle on an island surroundedby crystal clear waters, whose magnificent construction expressed the wealth and artistry of my people... At that time I also employed a young magician named Zargon at my court, who used to entertain me from time to time with his tricks. He was talented , very talented, in fact, but I would never have suspected that he lived in a secretchamber in the basement of my castle - a room in which he carried out all his magical experiments: he was obsessed with the crazy idea of artificially producing gold, which he urgently needed, in order to be able to pay for the lessons he took from the highest magicians in our country. One day, however, his wishes came true: he was accepted into the Seventh Circle of the Mages Guild, which meant that his full magical power had developed and he was entitled to use even the most powerful spells - yes, he eventually became even more powerful than his former teachers who now followed the development of their most gifted student with great concern - but in his infinite ambition he wanted even more: He wanted my throne! But instead of fighting my noble knights in a brave and fair fight, he turned to his magical powers and created an army of cruel, undead creatures... One dark night - there was a thunderstorm as if the Day of Judgment had dawned - He gathered these spawns of hell in front of my castle, and when the clock on the tower struck midnight, - what a macabre irony of fate - the corpses of my ancestors, who had been laid to rest in a crypt beneath the castle chambers, rose from theirs coffins - and opened the gates! It was little trouble for Zargon and his henchmen to take the castle within a few minutes: no one had expected this attack- a fatal mistake... After breaking down the door to my bedchamber, Zargon's blackbloods led me away to their master, who, without a word of explanation or apology, drove the blade of his sword up to the hilt into my chest..."

358.text: The king nods in agreement. "You're right: We have no more time to lose!", he decides, "The time has come to fight back, bring Zargon to justice and free the inhabitants of my kingdom from his tyranny! As you can see..." - he looks down sadly - "...unfortunately my supernatural appearance no longer allows me to challenge Zargon personally and atone for the mischief he has brought on us all, but maybe you are strong and smart enough To at least try! No! Don't say anything now! Don't contradict me: This isn't just any job - it's your destiny!" King Richard looks at you with pleading eyes...

362.text: You tell the stranger behind the hatch about your journey to this world and ask him if he could give you something to eat and a place to spend the night. Surprisingly, he doesn't seem to doubt your story in the slightest: "Of course I could...", the voice behind the door drawled, "But only on one condition: If I help you, you must promise me a small service as well "There is a small, of course not too dangerous, task that has to be done tomorrow. If you sign me a short written declaration that you will do it for me, I will in return give you a bed to sleep on , warm clothes and a warm supper." With these words, the man hands you a strangely already pre-formulated contract and a small, sharp little knife through the hatch. When you ask why you need the knife, the stranger replies indifferently: "I'm just being careful - too many people have already betrayed me! Therefore you will sign our agreement in the same blood that you will shed, should you dare, to break them..."

Well, now it's time for you to fulfill your part of our agreement: There is an evil elf king named Firon, who hides with his horde in his ice palace in the northwest of our beloved country. However, he often raids our small, peaceful village with his yeti army and plunders it - a few years ago he even reduced it completely to rubble. As head of the village council, I command you: stop him! Here are some clothes you will need to survive in the cold ice regions and a flask with a magic elixir that will make you invisible for a few seconds : Definitely don't use it unless you absolutely have to because, as said before, it will only protect you for one hit and you can only use it once! Now go on your way and put an end to Firon's dark machinations: May Zargon protect you...!" 389.text: You give the child the crystal ball so that he finally has something to play with - and above all, so that no one gets hurt during his games. With trembling fingers he touches the shimmering gem and looks at it as if the little ball were the most valuable thing in this world. "It's beautiful - what do you want for it?" it asks, afraid that he hasn't hoarded enough treasures in his young life and therefore has to give you the new toy back. "Nothing. I'll give it to you. But don't try to play football with it!" you replied kindly - happy to be able to make the child a little happier. The little thing stares at you with unbelieving eyes: "Really - nothing at all?" he repeats questioningly, as if he couldn't believe you. "Really - nothing at all!" you answer. The child, overjoyed, falls on your neck: "You're my friend!" he crows in his childlike joy, which has nothing of the hostile tone in which orcs and humans normally interact with each other, "Come with me: I will show you our cave and introduce you to my parents!" Before you can say anything back, the little one lets go of you and stalks into the undergrowth. Shaking your head, you follow the child through the thick undergrowth on the southern edge of the clearing, on a path that only the orcs know...

390.text: "Ah, so you've decided to buy one of our dog sleds?" the salesman asks you busily and then looks at your outstretched hand offering him the few silver coins you found in the dwarf mine. "Well...: Well, for the price I can't offer you our most exclusive and expensive model, of course, but I still think you'll be satisfied with it." He takes the coins, counts them and puts them in a small iron chest on the counter. "The sledge is being prepared for you. Thank you - and please recommend us to others!", he recites his well-rehearsed saying as a farewell and then turns back to his work behind the counter.
